newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PM SEES 1997 INFLATION AT 11 TO 12 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: PM SEES 1997 INFLATION AT 11 TO 12 PERCENT.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that he expected inflation in 1997 to be 11 to 12 percent and that the rate will fall below ten percent in 1998.
"Inflation this year (should)...reach 11 to 12 percent," Vagnorius said at a news conference.
"The rate should fall below ten percent next year," he added.
The government said in a statement on Wednesday that statistics department data suggested that inflation would be 11.5 percent this year if energy prices are raised.
Inflation fell sharply in 1996 to 13.1 percent from 35.7 percent in 1995.
Vagnorius added that it would not be good for the economy if inflation fell too quickly but did not explain why such a scenario would be a cause for concern.
"I wouldn't be very happy if monthly inflation was less than 0.6 percent...It would be slightly dangerous for our economy if inflation fell abruptly this year to seven percent," he said.
